description.text: Livestock Consolidation Research Act of 2026 This bill requires the Department of Agriculture's (USDA's) Economic Research Service (ERS) to publish a report on consolidation and concentration in the livestock industry (i.e., beef, dairy, pork, and poultry production, including broilers, eggs, and turkeys). ERS must publish the report within one year of the Census of Agriculture being made publicly available. As background, USDA's National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) conducts the census every five years. NASS released the 2022 census in 2024. The ERS report must include (1) information on changes in the size and location of ranches, farms, processing facilities, and packers throughout the United States; and (2) the impact of these changes on farmers, ranchers, and downstream consumers.

latestAction.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.

impact.summary: The bill requires USDA's Economic Research Service to publish after each Census a report on consolidation in beef, dairy, pork, and poultry. ERS must use NASS, FSIS, and AMS Packers and Stockyards data to analyze effects on ranchers, farmers, processing facilities, packers, and downstream consumers.

aiDescription.summary: The bill directs USDA's Economic Research Service to publish, within one year after each Census of Agriculture release, a report on consolidation and concentration in the livestock industry. It must cover beef, dairy, pork, and poultry (broilers, eggs, turkeys), track facility and herd changes, and assess producer and consumer impacts.
